exercises.hint: AND in SQL = && inside one filter() callback.
exercises.task: This SQL combines two filters: SELECT name FROM students WHERE gpa >= 3.0 AND program = 'Software Development'. Same result in JS.

exercises.hint: ORDER BY ... DESC LIMIT 2 = sort descending, then slice(0, 2). Use slice() first so you don't mutate the original array.
exercises.solution:
const students = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Morolake', program: 'Software Development', gpa: 3.8 },
  { id: 2, name: 'Tega', program: 'Network Security', gpa: 3.2 },
  { id: 3, name: 'Ama', program: 'Software Development', gpa: 2.9 },
  { id: 4, name: 'Liam', program: 'Data Science', gpa: 3.6 },
  { id: 5, name: 'Priya', program: 'Software Development', gpa: 3.9 },
  { id: 6, name: 'Noah', program: 'Network Security', gpa: 2.4 },
];

const names = students
  .slice()
  .sort((a, b) => b.gpa - a.gpa)
  .slice(0, 2)
  .map(s => s.name);
console.log(JSON.stringify(names));
exercises.task: This SQL sorts and trims: SELECT name FROM students ORDER BY gpa DESC LIMIT 2. Get the top two names in JS.

exercises.hint: A Set keeps only the first occurrence of each value — that's DISTINCT.
exercises.task: This SQL dedupes: SELECT DISTINCT program FROM students. Get the unique program names in JS.
